_doc: Street-grid block fill. d00-structure lays the arterial lattice, paving and perimeter trees/lamps for every block, but only 6 of the 21 core blocks were ever claimed by a district — the rest render as bare concrete lots at play zoom. This fills grid block r1c4, the emptiest (12% sprite coverage measured in the real renderer). Buildings are PINNED landmarks, not scattered: pass E's scatter is occupancy-aware but has no row aligner, so letting it pick building_shell produced a novelty ice-cream kiosk and a giant mushroom at random baselines instead of a street wall. Compile: python3 scripts/compile-exterior-district.py --spec data/city-specs/biome-specs/blocks/d29-midtown-retail.json --qa -v. Vocabulary: data/limezu-visual-catalog/placement-rules.json. Format: docs/EXTERIOR-COMPILER.md
_layout_doc: TWO RULES this spec learned the hard way, both silent 'no accepting surface / overlaps a claim' rejections. (1) LATTICE: every landmark x/y and every keep_clear rect must be a multiple of 16. An off-lattice x like 280 makes the collider band start mid-cell, so it bleeds into the neighbouring cell and trips is_free. (2) HALO: pass C claims each shell's sprite rect PLUS a 16px halo on all sides, so a row must advance by sprite_width + 32 to leave a clear cell between claims. Vertical bands are chosen so scattered props never sit where a building sprite will draw over them: props live at y256-288 and y400-448, the rows occupy y64-240 and y464-592.

compiler._doc: coords 'local': every rect/point is relative to bbox. Grid block r1c4 sits between arterials x2560/x3392 and y1200/y1872.
